title: Avo-7-part-3
description: Avionics examination covering pitot-static systems, air data computers, airspeed indicators, altimeters, vertical speed indicators, atmospheric pressure, temperature sensing, and pitot-static system testing.

questions.question: In Air data system, Airspeed Indicator is calculated by Airdata Computer.
options: C. Only the altimeter is calculated by the Air Data Computer
questions.explanation: The Air Data Computer processes pitot and static pressure information and calculates airspeed and other air data parameters.

questions.question: Use of CADC help minimize the 'plumbing' arrangements of pitot static system.
options: C. Only electrical wiring is reduced
questions.explanation: A Central Air Data Computer reduces the need for extensive individual pressure plumbing by centralizing air-data processing.

questions.question: Not correct about pitot probe inspection:
options: A. Inspect for blockage and damage
B. Check the probe for contamination
C. No problem nicks on the leading edge of the pitot probe and even pitot probe axis.
questions.explanation: Nicks or damage on the leading edge or axis of a pitot probe can affect pressure sensing and therefore must not be ignored.

questions.question: Which of the following is not correct about the static tube?
options: A. The static tube is open at its forward end, but has a series of small holes drilled circumferentially at a calculated distance from the forward end.
B. Static pressure is sensed through specially positioned openings.
C. Static ports provide ambient static pressure.
questions.explanation: A static tube is designed with static sensing openings rather than being simply open at its forward end in the manner described.

questions.question: Which one is/are the deflecting element for airspeed indicator?
options: A. Pitot connection and static connection
questions.explanation: The airspeed indicator responds to the pressure difference supplied through its pitot and static connections.

questions.question: Lag errors are caused by the fact that any changes in the static or dynamic pressure outside the aircraft require a finite amount of time to make their way down the tubing and affect the gauges.
options: B. Only electrical systems have lag errors
questions.explanation: Pressure changes take a finite time to travel through pitot-static plumbing, causing an indication delay known as lag error.

questions.question: Vertical speed Indicator is designed to indicate the rate of altitude change from the change of static pressure alone.
options: C. It uses only dynamic pressure
questions.explanation: The VSI detects the rate of change of static pressure and converts it into an indication of climb or descent rate.

questions.question: The static pressure for vertical speed indicator goes to the diaphragm and the case of the instrument.
options: C. It goes only to the diaphragm
questions.explanation: Static pressure is applied directly to the diaphragm while also entering the instrument case through a calibrated restriction.

questions.question: The complexity of a pitot-static system depends primarily upon:
options: B. The type and size of aircraft and the number of locations at which primary flight instrument data are required
questions.explanation: Larger and more complex aircraft generally require more pitot-static sources and distribution arrangements.

questions.question: The airspeed indicated on airspeed indicator is relative to the surrounding of air molecules.
options: C. It is relative only to aircraft altitude
questions.explanation: Airspeed is the speed of the aircraft relative to the surrounding air mass.

questions.question: In instantaneous VSI, when the aircraft pitches up it indicates:
questions.explanation: When the aircraft pitches up and begins climbing, the instantaneous VSI responds to the resulting pressure change and indicates a climb.

questions.question: In aircraft that has independent separate pitot-static tube leak check done:
options: C. Only the altimeter needs checking
questions.explanation: Where separate independent pitot-static systems are installed, the applicable systems must be checked for leakage.

questions.question: In some CADC the pressure sensing and transducer is by means of silicon diaphragm containing piezoelectric element.
options: C. It uses only a mechanical spring
questions.explanation: Some air data computers use semiconductor pressure transducers employing silicon diaphragms and piezoelectric or piezoresistive sensing elements.

questions.question: As we go up atmospheric pressure decrease, the reason is:
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude because gravity causes the density and weight of the air above to decrease.

questions.question: True altitude is the actual elevation above mean sea level.
options: B. Only pressure altitude is measured above sea level
questions.explanation: True altitude is the actual vertical height of the aircraft above mean sea level.

questions.question: Indicated altitude is the reading on the altimeter when it is set to the local barometric pressure at mean sea level.
options: C. It is always equal to pressure altitude
questions.explanation: Indicated altitude is the altitude shown by the altimeter according to its current barometric setting.

questions.question: What could be the issue if the standby altimeter doesn't operate correctly?
options: A. Check the fuel quantity sensor only
B. Check for water plugs in alternate static ports, inspect pitot probe for damage or debris.
C. Check only the engine oil pressure
questions.explanation: Blocked alternate static ports or damaged/contaminated pitot probes can cause incorrect standby instrument indications.

questions.question: Which of the following is not correct about the pipeline of pitot static system?
options: A. The chosen diameter of pipeline is related to the amount of pressure that goes to the instruments.
B. Plumbing dimensions affect pressure transmission characteristics.
C. Pipeline diameter has no relationship to the pressure system design.
questions.explanation: The provided answer identifies the statement about pipeline diameter and pressure as the incorrect statement.

questions.question: The pressure-sensing element of altimeter is:
questions.explanation: An altimeter uses aneroid capsules that expand and contract as static atmospheric pressure changes.

questions.question: Sensing element in airspeed and vertical speed indicator:
questions.explanation: Diaphragms are pressure-sensitive elements used in both airspeed and vertical speed instruments.

questions.question: Which of the following is not correct about drain traps of pitot static system?
options: A. Drain valves are used to remove accumulated moisture.
B. Drain valves help prevent water accumulation in the system.
C. The drain valves are not of the self-closing type so that they can be inadvertently left in the open position after drainage of accumulated water.
questions.explanation: Pitot-static drain valves are designed so that they close properly; leaving a drain open could cause pressure leakage.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct?
options: A. Heater C/B can't be closed.
B. Heater C/B must always remain open.
C. Pitot heaters do not use circuit breakers.
questions.explanation: The provided source answer is that the heater circuit breaker can't be closed.

questions.question: The type of altimeter with electronics that can send encoded altimeter data for ATC altitude is:
questions.explanation: An encoded altimeter provides altitude information in an electrical coded form for transmission to ATC equipment.

questions.question: System/component doesn't need heating:
questions.explanation: Pitot probes and some temperature probes may require anti-icing heat, while a static port does not normally have a heater.

questions.question: Pitot tube measure:
options: A. Dynamic and static pressure (total pressure)
questions.explanation: A pitot probe senses total pressure, which consists of static pressure plus dynamic pressure.

questions.question: Subsonic aircraft have pitot mounted:
options: B. Under wing, around nose fuselage and vertical stab.
questions.explanation: Pitot probes on subsonic aircraft may be installed under the wing, around the nose fuselage, or near the vertical stabilizer depending on aircraft design.

questions.question: Pitot system measure dynamic pressure created by forward motion of aircraft and static pressure of speed, altitude and vertical speed.
questions.explanation: The pitot-static system provides the pressure information used to determine airspeed, altitude, and vertical speed.

questions.question: Static pressure from vent static ports is guided into:
options: B. The casing surrounding the diaphragm / aneroid of altimeter
questions.explanation: Static pressure is routed to the case surrounding the aneroid capsules in a conventional altimeter.

questions.question: TAT used by ADC to calculate TAT, SAT, TAS.
options: C. It calculates fuel flow only
questions.explanation: The Air Data Computer uses total air temperature along with pressure and other air-data information to calculate parameters such as SAT and TAS.

questions.question: What could be the reason for altimeter error?
options: A. Variation in temperature and pressure
questions.explanation: Temperature and atmospheric pressure variations can produce errors in altitude indication if not properly accounted for.

questions.question: Which of the following is not correct about Digital Air Data Computer (DADC)?
options: A. A DADC processes air data electronically.
B. A DADC usually receives its data in analog form.
C. A DADC can calculate several air data parameters.
questions.explanation: The provided answer identifies the statement that a DADC usually receives its data in analog form as the incorrect statement.

questions.question: At greater heights the atmosphere is divided into further layers which from the tropopause upwards are termed as:
questions.explanation: The provided source identifies the layers above the tropopause as ozonosphere, ionosphere, and exosphere.

questions.question: Which uses both static and pitot pressure?
questions.explanation: The airspeed indicator compares pitot total pressure with static pressure to determine indicated airspeed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of metering unit in the vertical speed indicator?
options: C. To slow down the rate at which pressure can change within the air flight instrument case.
questions.explanation: The calibrated restriction in the VSI slows pressure equalization between the case and diaphragm, allowing the instrument to measure pressure change rate.

questions.question: The port which sends air pressure to vertical speed indicator:
questions.explanation: The VSI operates from static pressure supplied through the aircraft's static system.

questions.question: Where is the location of pitot probe for commercial aircraft?
options: A. Around the nose section of aircraft.
questions.explanation: Commercial aircraft commonly locate pitot probes around the nose where the airflow is suitable for accurate total-pressure measurement.

questions.question: The temperature of atmosphere above tropopause is:
questions.explanation: In the standard atmosphere, the temperature near the tropopause is approximately -56.5°C.

questions.question: If the standby altimeter is inoperative the problem is:
options: A. Alternate pitot or static system.
questions.explanation: An inoperative standby altimeter may indicate a problem with the alternate pitot-static system supplying it.

questions.question: At the point of stagnation the KE is converted into:
questions.explanation: At a stagnation point, the velocity of the airflow becomes zero and kinetic energy is converted into pressure energy.

questions.question: The number of pressure connectors to the CADC:
questions.explanation: The provided source answer specifies three pressure connectors to the CADC.

questions.question: Altitude in terms of the distance above a certain point is:
questions.explanation: Height is the vertical distance between an aircraft and a specified reference point or surface.

questions.question: Pressure altitude is:
options: A. The actual elevation above terrain
B. The air pressure in terms of altitude in the International Standard Atmosphere.
C. The temperature above mean sea level
questions.explanation: Pressure altitude is the altitude corresponding to a particular atmospheric pressure according to the International Standard Atmosphere.

questions.question: Absolute altitude is:
options: A. The height of the aircraft above the terrain over which it is flying.
B. The height above mean sea level only
C. The pressure altitude at standard pressure
questions.explanation: Absolute altitude refers to the aircraft's vertical height above the terrain directly below it.

questions.question: Where is the typical location of pressure heads of subsonic aircraft?
options: A. Inside the engine nacelle only
B. Ahead of wing tip, at the side of a fuselage nose section or ahead of vertical stabilizer.
questions.explanation: Pitot pressure heads are positioned in areas where the airflow provides suitable pressure measurement, such as ahead of wing tips, near the fuselage nose, or ahead of the vertical stabilizer.

questions.question: Which of the following is not the procedure applied on pitot static heater system?
options: A. Make sure as pitot probe is covered by plastic.
B. Follow the applicable aircraft maintenance procedure.
C. Check the heater operation as specified by maintenance instructions.
questions.explanation: Covering a heated pitot probe with plastic is not an appropriate operating procedure because the heater can damage the cover and create a hazard.

questions.question: TAT probe measures the temperature of airflow over airplane and changes to analogue electrical signal.
questions.explanation: A TAT probe senses total air temperature and provides an electrical signal corresponding to the measured temperature.

questions.question: Airspeed indicator use:
questions.explanation: The airspeed indicator operates from the difference between total pitot pressure and static pressure.

questions.question: If both pressure equal in vertical speed indicator will read:
questions.explanation: When pressure inside and outside the VSI diaphragm is equal, there is no pressure differential and the indication is zero.

questions.question: Which of the following doesn't change with position error?
questions.explanation: The provided answer identifies the vertical speed indicator as not changing with position error.

questions.question: Which one of the following indicates the relation between ram air and static air?
questions.explanation: Indicated airspeed is derived from the relationship between total/ram pressure and static pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct procedure for pitot system leak check?
options: A. Make sure that the ATC transponders are in standby mode.
B. Turn all radios to maximum power.
questions.explanation: During a pitot-static leak check, applicable aircraft systems such as ATC transponders must be placed in the required standby condition according to the maintenance procedure.

questions.question: ADC calculates static air temperature (SAT) from TAT data it gets from TAT probe.
options: C. ADC uses fuel temperature instead
questions.explanation: The ADC uses TAT probe information together with airspeed and other parameters to determine static air temperature.

questions.question: To prevent the entry of water and other foreign matter, the pitot pressure tube is provided with:
questions.explanation: Baffles inside or around the pitot probe help prevent water and foreign matter from entering the pressure line.

questions.question: Ram air pressure from the aircraft's pitot tube is directed into:
options: B. A diaphragm in an analog airspeed instrument case
questions.explanation: In a conventional airspeed indicator, pitot pressure is applied to the diaphragm while static pressure surrounds it in the instrument case.

questions.question: Airspeed indicators are in effect very sensitive pressure gauge measuring the difference between pitot and static pressure.
questions.explanation: An airspeed indicator is essentially a sensitive differential pressure instrument comparing pitot and static pressure.

questions.question: In instantaneous VSI when the aircraft pitches down:
questions.explanation: Pitching down causes the aircraft to descend, and an instantaneous VSI responds by indicating a rate of descent.

questions.question: Which one is correct?
options: A. Direct indication and transmission of data highly affected to error due to plumbing.
B. Plumbing has no effect on pressure measurements.
C. Only electrical wiring causes all air data errors.
questions.explanation: Pitot-static plumbing can introduce errors due to leakage, restriction, lag, moisture, and other pressure-transmission effects.

questions.question: Which one is used to remove accumulation of moisture in pipe?
questions.explanation: Drain holes or drain valves are provided to remove accumulated moisture from pitot-static plumbing.

questions.question: Static port blocked affects:
questions.explanation: A blocked static port can affect the airspeed indicator, vertical speed indicator, and altimeter because all depend on static pressure.

questions.question: Pressure sensing element increased sensitivity in ALT:
questions.explanation: Stacking aneroid capsules increases the effective pressure-sensitive area and improves the sensitivity of the altimeter mechanism.

questions.question: Which one is correct about a pressurized aircraft?
options: A. Cabin pressure & outside pressure are different.
B. Cabin pressure and outside pressure are always identical.
C. Outside pressure does not change with altitude.
questions.explanation: In a pressurized aircraft, the cabin is maintained at a higher pressure than the surrounding atmosphere at cruising altitude.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about pitot static port?
options: A. Pitot port is closed and static port is forward open.
B. Pitot port is forward open & static closed.
C. Both ports are completely closed.
questions.explanation: The pitot port faces the airflow and is open to sense total pressure, while static ports are arranged to sense ambient static pressure without directly facing the airflow.

questions.question: The diameter of pitot depends on:
questions.explanation: The provided source answer identifies the length as a factor related to pitot diameter.

questions.question: Ram air for air speed indicator supplied for:
options: A. Instrument case, static air for diaphragm
B. Diaphragm, static air for instrument case
C. Both pressures for the instrument case only
questions.explanation: In a conventional airspeed indicator, ram/total pressure from the pitot tube is applied to the diaphragm, while static pressure surrounds the diaphragm in the instrument case.

questions.question: Onboard aircraft equipment subject to pitot static testing:
options: B. Fuel quantity indicator, tachometer, EGT
C. Compass, fuel gauge, oil pressure gauge
questions.explanation: The altimeter, airspeed indicator, and vertical speed indicator are primary instruments connected to the pitot-static system and are subject to pitot-static testing.
